title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: MARISOL'S SKY
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Marisol Vega, a night cashier at a truck stop in Las Cruces, New Mexico.
For nineteen years, she sold coffee and beef jerky under the best night sky in America.
She had never once looked at it.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE COFFEE MUG
segments.quote: Remember to look up at the stars and not down at your feet.
segments.author: Stephen Hawking
lines: One night at three a.m., she sat out back, adding up bills.
Cecil, an old trucker, sat down with his mug. It had words from Stephen Hawking on it:
Remember to look up at the stars and not down at your feet.
So she looked up. Oh my.
That Saturday, she bought a yard sale telescope. Forty bucks.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE LAUGHING BOSS
segments.quote: Never be limited by other people's limited imaginations.
segments.author: Mae Jemison
lines: Her boss Dale laughed. Marisol, you sell jerky.
Then, in a library book, she found the astronaut Mae Jemison:
Never be limited by other people's limited imaginations.
She kept going.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE WATER TOWER
segments.quote: I learned very early the difference between knowing the name of something and knowing something.
segments.author: Richard Feynman
lines: She memorized fifty star names, and bragged to Cecil. He said, show me one.
She proudly aimed. For twenty minutes, they admired a radio tower.
That night she read the scientist Richard Feynman:
I learned very early the difference between knowing the name of something and knowing something.
She went outside to learn the real sky, one star at a time.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE NOTEBOOK
segments.quote: Attention is the beginning of devotion.
segments.author: Mary Oliver
lines: She wanted Saturn. But weeks of clouds rolled in.
Her neighbor Mrs. Romero read her a line from the writer Mary Oliver:
Attention is the beginning of devotion.
So every night, same hour, she drew what she saw in a notebook.
One August night, there it was. Tiny rings. She yelled so loud, two dogs woke up.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE NACHOS
segments.quote: Mingle the starlight with your lives and you won't be fretted by trifles.
segments.author: Maria Mitchell
lines: Then came a bad week. Worn-out brakes. A man screaming about nacho cheese.
She was ready to scream back, until she remembered the astronomer Maria Mitchell:
Mingle the starlight with your lives and you won't be fretted by trifles.
She stepped outside for two minutes. Saturn was still there.
She came back and smiled. He got extra cheese.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: FREE STARS
segments.quote: For small creatures such as we the vastness is bearable only through love.
segments.author: Carl Sagan
lines: But she was out there alone, and it felt awful big.
Mrs. Romero lent her a novel by Carl Sagan, with one line circled:
For small creatures such as we the vastness is bearable only through love.
So she painted a sign for the parking lot. Free stars.
Truckers lined up at two a.m. Dale looked for a long time, and whispered, that's real?

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Look up. Ignore doubters. Learn it. Pay attention. Let small things go. Share it.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Look up. Ignore doubters. Learn the real thing. Pay attention. Let small stuff go. Share what you love.
I bought a telescope once. I watched the lens cap for an hour.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
